newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi plays down new decree on foreign journalists.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi plays down new decree on foreign journalists.

text.p: Vietnam said on Thursday a new decree listing controls on foreign journalists simply formalised existing regulations and demonstrated the government's policy of ensuring they work under favourable conditions.

"Basically, the decree systematises existing regulations... at the same time supplementing and further clarifying some specific issues relevant to the new circumstances," Foreign Ministry spokesman Tran Quang Hoan told a news conference.
The decree comes during mounting concern about strict limits on foreign correspondents operating in the communist country.
Last week, Hanoi refused to renew a residency visa for an American correspondent of the Far Eastern Economic Review magazine, effectively expelling him.
The regulations, which will come into effect on December 1, include a stipulation that foreign correspondents should apply for permission to carry out press activities five days in advance.
Asked whether this rule would include covering major or urgent news events, Hoan said it was one of the issues which would be tackled in an inter-ministerial circular on the decree.
The decree would also require correspondents, for the first time, to carry foreign press cards. These would be valid for six months and may be extended by the foreign ministry.
Vietnam opened its door to foreign correspondents in the late 1980s, allowing a number of overseas news organisations to establish bureaux in the capital, Hanoi.
But despite an obscure and previously unpublished system of regulations, media activities have remained tightly controlled.
Foreign journalists are seldom invited to news conferences, interviews with senior officials are rare, permission must be obtained for travel and staff must be hired from the government.
